description: The canonical governance baseline: the GOV-* guardrails every cloud account and project lives under, and how each cloud enforces them. Defined in 00_UniversalStandards/08_Governance_Guardrails.md. Vendored into consumer repos as .playbook/schemas/governance_baseline.v1.json; Genesis reads it and implements each control per cloud, so the guardrails have one source of truth and cannot drift. mode is each control's target state at the organization root: enforce blocks violations, dry_run only logs them. Genesis stages every new or changed control in dry run first and promotes it to its target only after the dry-run log is clean or every violation has an approved exception. A target changes only through a reviewed change to this file.

controls.intent: No default networks; every network is declared in IaC.

aws.note: No SCP can prevent default VPCs; account vending deletes them in every region.

controls.intent: No long-lived workload keys; workloads use federated, short-lived identity.
No public IPs on VMs; egress goes through NAT, ingress through load balancers.

aws.note: S3 account-level Block Public Access is set at vending; the SCP stops it being turned off.

controls.intent: Access to storage is IAM-only; no object or bucket ACLs.

aws.note: New buckets default to Object Ownership BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled); SEC-002 checks it at plan time.

controls.intent: Resources are created only in approved regions.
Access is granted only to identities in the platform's own directory.

gcp.note: Needs the organization's directory customer ID; stays dry_run until it is set.

aws.note: Resource policies are checked for aws:PrincipalOrgID at plan time (rig-scan); RAM sharing outside the organization is denied here.

controls.intent: VMs cannot act as routers; routing is declared in the network layer.

aws.note: Denies turning off SourceDestCheck through ModifyInstanceAttribute or ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute; exceptions per account for appliance VMs.

controls.intent: No network side channels between projects or accounts; traffic goes through the platform network.

gcp.note: Managed services with private IP (e.g. Cloud SQL) use peering and need a project-scoped exception.

controls.intent: Audit logging is always on and cannot be disabled from inside an account or project.

gcp.note: Admin Activity logs are always on. Genesis sets an org-level audit config (Data Access logs for IAM, KMS, Secret Manager, Storage, not allServices) and an org log sink to the governance project; projects cannot remove org-level config.

aws.note: An organization trail is created in the governance account.

controls.intent: Default service accounts get no automatic roles.

aws.note: AWS has no default service accounts with automatic grants.

controls.intent: Interactive VM access goes through IAM, never through distributed SSH keys.

aws.note: Interactive access uses SSM Session Manager.

controls.intent: Guardrails cannot be changed or escaped from inside an account or project.

gcp.note: Only the governance identity holds roles/orgpolicy.policyAdmin, granted at the organization; project owners cannot override org policies they do not administer.
